chunks: Ḥamdawayh ibn Nuṣayr narrated to me; he said: Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said: Ibn Muskān informed us, from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

Concerning a man who prays the two rakʿahs of al-Witr, then stands and forgets the tashahhud until he bows, then remembers while he is in rukuʿ, he said: “He should sit up from his bowing, then recite the tashahhud, then stand and complete [the prayer].” He said: I said, “Did you not say regarding the obligatory prayer that if he remembers after he has bowed, he proceeds, then performs two sajdahs after he finishes and recites the tashahhud in them?” So he said: “The supererogatory prayer is not like the obligatory prayer.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: “And whoever is forgetful regarding the recitation…” up to his statement: “And whoever recites a surah…”—the explanation of all of that has already passed. Then al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: “Whoever recites a surah after al-Ḥamd, then wishes to recite another in its place, he may cut it off and recite another so long as he has not gone beyond half of it in his recitation. But whoever recites ‘Qul huwa Allāhu Aḥad’ and ‘Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn’ has no right to go back from them.”

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدَ: the testimony recited in the sitting portion of salat
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the witr prayer, here referring to a night supererogatory prayer context
key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: being in the state of bowing (rukuʿ)
key_terms.سُورَةً: a chapter of the Qur'an recited in salat

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets the tashahhud in a supererogatory prayer and remembers during rukuʿ?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings on forgetfulness in salat, especially the difference between supererogatory and obligatory prayer. It states that if one forgets the tashahhud in a nafilah prayer and remembers during rukuʿ, he returns to sit for tashahhud and then completes the prayer. It also transmits a ruling from al-Shaykh regarding changing a surah during recitation before passing its halfway point, with an exception for specific surahs.
